flags.evidence: Opened page/index.html from disk in Chromium at 1440x900 (dsf 1) and 390x844 (dsf 3). At 1440 the most prominent first-screen action is the filled hero button 'Reserve a place' (a.btn-light, href #reserve); it is not in the first screen at 390. Clicking it scrolls to the #reserve section ('Reserve a place.'), whose only control is the 'Hold my place' submit button. Before submitting, the section says 'Deposits aren't open yet, so there's nothing to pay today. Leave your email and we'll hold your place in line.', the hero small print says 'you can hold a place with your email today', and the button note says 'No charge. No newsletter. Only notes about Morrow.' Nothing on the page says the address is not sent or recorded; the disclosures cover only money and deposits. Typed buyer@mail.example and clicked 'Hold my place' at both widths: the panel 'Your place is held. We've noted buyer@mail.example. You'll get one email when the $20 deposit opens, and another whenever the plan changes. That's it.' appeared, with zero network requests after the click, no page errors, and the address only in the visitor's own localStorage key 'morrow.held'. The inline script sets var HOLD_ENDPOINT = '' and the fetch runs only if it is truthy (its own comment says the mailing list is not connected). The page therefore reports success (a held place and promised emails) for something that did not happen, without saying so before the visitor acted. The brief supplies no collection endpoint, so no 'Does not count' exception applies, and this is the primary action, not a secondary link.
